summary: Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. He holds a post as Lecturer at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Vladimir Balabushevich (1900–1970) was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1970 and 1990).

Vladimir Minorsky (1877–1966) studied at Moscow Imperial University and the Lazarev Institute of Oriental Languages. A specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history, he held posts at INALCO (~1923–1932) and SOAS University of London (~1932–1944).

Vladimir Tikhonov is a historian and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, Korea University, and Moscow State University. He lectured at Kyung Hee University before joining the University of Oslo in 2000.

Tibetologist Volker Caumanns completed his MA at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He has held positions at Munich, LIRI, Bern, Hamburg, and Leipzig.

Volker Grabowsky studied at Kiel University and Chiang Mai University. A historian, he held posts at the University of Passau, National University of Laos, University of Münster, and the University of Hamburg, where he became chair professor in 2009.

Volker Zotz studied at the University of Vienna and under Anagarika Govinda. Working in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at the University of Vienna, Otani and Ryukoku universities, Saarland University, and the University of Luxembourg.

Vrajavallabha Dvivedi (1926–2012) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as head of the Yogatantra Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as Deputy Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–1992).
Vriti Sharma works in the fields of computational studies and Indology. She has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.
W. F. Jayasuriya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

W. H. D. Rouse (1863–1950) studied at Cheltenham College, Regent's Park College, and Christ's College, Cambridge. An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Bedford School, Cheltenham, and Rugby, and was headmaster of The Perse School (1902–1928).

W. H. R. Rivers (1864–1922) studied at Tonbridge School, St Bartholomew's, and the University of London. Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held medical and academic posts at Cambridge, University College London, and St John's College.

W. Norman Brown (1892–1975) earned degrees at Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton. An Indologist and historian, he held posts at Johns Hopkins, Prince of Wales College, and the University of Pennsylvania (~1926–1966).

W. Randolph Kloetzli earned his PhD at the University of Chicago and worked in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including J. A. B. van Buitenen and lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held a professorship at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and served as Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Wai-lun Tam is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He became a professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walpola Rahula (1907–1997) studied at Vidyalankara Pirivena, Calcutta, Ceylon, and Paris. Specializing in Buddhist studies and history, he served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (1964–1969) and professor at Northwestern University (1964).

Walter Bruno Henning (1908–1967) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. After studying at the University of Göttingen, he held academic posts at SOAS University of London (~1936–1961), Columbia University, and UC Berkeley (~1961–1967).

Walter Elliot (1803–1887) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the East India Company College and the College of Fort St George, later serving as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in Madras (1837–1842).

Walter Eugene Clark (1881–1960) earned his doctorate at Harvard and studied under Richard Pischel. A scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, he taught at the University of Chicago before serving as Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard (1927–1950).
